questions.question: The term ‘banana kick’ is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Football**__

• A banana kick is a type of kick that curves or bends in the air, typically used in free kicks and corner kicks.
 
• This technique is often used to navigate around defensive walls or to place the ball into the goal from a challenging angle.
 
• Famous footballers known for their banana kicks include legends like **David Beckham** and **Roberto Carlos**.

• The physics behind a banana kick involves imparting spin to the ball, resulting in a curved trajectory due to the **Magnus effect**.
 
• Mastering the banana kick requires significant skill, practice, and an understanding of ball dynamics.
 
• This technique adds a strategic element to the game, allowing players to create scoring opportunities from set pieces.

questions.question: The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022, received the assent of the President on ________.

• **The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022** received the assent of the President on **Tue Jan 31 2023 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**.
 
• The Act aims to provide an effective legal framework to combat piracy and ensure the safety and security of maritime trade routes.
 
• It defines piracy and prescribes stringent punishments for those involved in such activities.
 
• The Act aligns with India's commitment to international conventions and treaties on maritime safety and security.

• The Act extends to the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of India and applies to all persons irrespective of their nationality.
 
• The legislation also provides for the establishment of designated courts for the speedy trial of piracy-related offenses.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Pala Dynasty of eastern India is INCORRECT?

options.text: Devapala was the grandson of Gopala.
The Pala kings were the followers of Buddhism.
The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala founded the Valabhi university**__

__
 
• **Dharmapala founded the Vikramashila University**, not the Valabhi university.
 
• The Pala Dynasty was an important ruling dynasty in eastern India, particularly in the regions of Bengal and Bihar.
 
• Devapala, the third ruler of the Pala Dynasty, was indeed the grandson of Gopala, the dynasty's founder.
 
• The Pala kings were notable patrons of Buddhism and played a significant role in the spread of Mahayana Buddhism in Tibet.
 
• Gopala, who founded the Pala dynasty, came to power around the mid-8th century CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Pala Dynasty is known for its contributions to the art, culture, and architecture of Bengal and Bihar regions.
 
• The dynasty's name "Pala" means "protector" and was used as a suffix to the names of all Pala monarchs.
 
• Dharmapala, one of the most prominent rulers of the Pala Dynasty, was instrumental in establishing the Pala influence over northern India.
 
• The Pala period is often regarded as a high point in the history of Bengal and Bihar, marked by prosperity and cultural flourishing.
 
• The Pala rulers were also known for their military prowess and diplomatic relations with other regional powers.

questions.question: Which of the following folk music of Chhattisgarh is based on the epic Mahabharata?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandavani**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandavani** is a traditional folk music form from Chhattisgarh that is based on the epic **Mahabharata**.
 
• It is a narrative singing style where the performer enacts stories from the Mahabharata, often accompanied by musical instruments such as the tambura and harmonium.
 
• This form of storytelling is characterized by its dramatic and expressive performance, where the singer uses both song and speech to convey the tales of the Pandavas.
 
• Pandavani is not just a musical performance but also a theatrical one, involving gestures, facial expressions, and sometimes even props.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandavani** performers often belong to the **Bhajan Mandali** tradition, which is a group dedicated to performing devotional songs and stories.
 
• One of the most renowned Pandavani performers is **Teejan Bai**, who has received numerous awards for her contribution to this art form, including the **Padma Shri** and **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• The art form has been instrumental in preserving the oral tradition of the Mahabharata in the region, making it accessible to the local populace.
 
• Pandavani performances are usually held during festivals, special occasions, and in village gatherings, serving as a form of entertainment as well as cultural education.

questions.question: Who developed the technique of preserving the quality of food by raising its temperature to prevent microbial growth in the food?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Louis Pasteur**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Louis Pasteur** developed the technique of preserving the quality of food by raising its temperature to prevent microbial growth in the food.
 
• This process is known as **pasteurization**, named after Louis Pasteur.
 
• Pasteurization involves heating the food to a specific temperature for a set period and then cooling it immediately.
 
• This technique is widely used in the dairy industry to extend the shelf life of milk and other dairy products.
 
• Besides dairy, pasteurization is also used for juices, canned foods, and various other consumables to ensure safety and longevity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Louis Pasteur** was a French biologist, microbiologist, and chemist renowned for his discoveries of the principles of vaccination, microbial fermentation, and pasteurization.
 
• His work in germ theory also led to significant advancements in the field of microbiology and the development of vaccines for diseases like rabies and anthrax.
 
• Pasteur's contributions have had a lasting impact on public health, food safety, and the overall understanding of microbiology.
 
• He is often regarded as one of the founders of modern microbiology.

questions.question: Which of the following is issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Certificates of deposits**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Certificates of deposits** are issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value.
 
• They are a type of time deposit with a fixed maturity date and specified interest rate.
 
• Certificates of deposits are negotiable instruments, meaning they can be transferred from one party to another.
 
• They are often used by banks to raise funds from the market.
 
• The interest rate on certificates of deposits is generally higher than that on regular savings accounts, making them an attractive investment option for large investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Promissory notes** are written promises to pay a certain amount of money at a future date but are not issued at a discount.
 
• **Commercial papers** are unsecured short-term debt instruments issued by corporations, not commercial banks.
 
• **Treasury bills** are short-term government securities issued at a discount but by the government, not commercial banks.

questions.question: The Green Revolution led to an increase in the agricultural output primarily due to the use of HYV seeds. Here, HYV refers to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Yielding Variety**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **High Yielding Variety (HYV)** refers to seeds that are engineered to produce more crops per area planted compared to traditional varieties.
 
• The introduction of **HYV seeds** was a crucial component of the Green Revolution, which significantly boosted agricultural productivity, particularly in developing countries.
 
• These seeds are often more resistant to pests and diseases and can grow in a variety of climatic conditions, making them highly adaptable.
 
• The use of **HYV seeds** typically requires the application of modern agricultural techniques, including the use of fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• While HYV seeds have contributed to increased food production, they also necessitate careful management to avoid issues such as soil degradation and water resource depletion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** began in the 1960s and was marked by the adoption of new agricultural technologies, including HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• It led to a substantial increase in food grain production, particularly in countries like India and Mexico.
 
• The Green Revolution played a significant role in transforming agriculture from subsistence farming to commercial farming, making many countries self-sufficient in food production.
 
• However, the Green Revolution also brought challenges such as environmental damage, increased inequality among farmers, and the marginalization of smallholders.

questions.question: Which of the following is the default alignment of text in a Microsoft Word document?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Left alignment** is the default alignment of text in a Microsoft Word document.
 
• In left-aligned text, the text is aligned with the left margin, and the right edge of the text is ragged.
 
• This alignment is commonly used for most documents as it provides a clean and organized look.
 
• Other alignment options in Microsoft Word include right, center, and justified, which can be selected based on the formatting requirements.
 
• Left alignment ensures that the text starts at the same point on the left side, making it easier to read and follow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microsoft Word** is a widely used word processing software developed by Microsoft.
 
• It offers various formatting tools to enhance the appearance of documents, including text alignment options.
 
• Users can change the text alignment by selecting the text and choosing the desired alignment option from the toolbar or the "Paragraph" settings.
 
• Understanding text alignment is essential for creating professional and well-structured documents.

questions.question: The proclamation of which Act by the King of England in 1773 paved the way for the establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first step taken by the British Government to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• This act marked the beginning of a parliamentary control over the company and introduced significant administrative reforms.
 
• One of the key provisions of the Regulating Act was the establishment of a **Supreme Court at Calcutta**, which was set up in 1774.
 
• The Supreme Court was intended to administer justice to British subjects in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• This act also laid the foundation for the subsequent acts and reforms in the Indian administrative structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Regulating Act** was passed by the British Parliament in 1773 to address the financial and administrative issues faced by the East India Company.
 
• It required the company to report its revenue and administrative activities to the British government.
 
• The act also established the office of the Governor-General of Bengal and created a council to assist the Governor-General.
 
• The Regulating Act was followed by other significant legislations such as the Pitt's India Act (1784), which further reformed the company's administration and brought it under stricter control of the British government.

• Ursa Major has been recognized and represented in various ways by different cultures, including Native American, Hindu, and Chinese traditions.
 
• The constellation is part of the family of constellations that includes Ursa Minor, Draco, and Boötes.

questions.question: Which Section of the Representation of People’s Act (RPA), 1951 deprives the prisoners of their right to vote?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 62 (5)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 62 (5)** of the Representation of People's Act, 1951, deprives prisoners of their right to vote.
 
• This section states that no person shall vote at any election if he is confined in a prison, whether under a sentence of imprisonment or transportation or otherwise, or is in the lawful custody of the police.
 
• The provision applies to all individuals in prison, irrespective of the nature of the crime or the duration of the sentence.
 
• However, this disqualification does not apply to those under preventive detention.
 
• The rationale behind this provision is to maintain the sanctity and security of the electoral process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Representation of People's Act, 1951** was enacted to provide for the conduct of elections to the Houses of Parliament and to the House or Houses of the Legislature of each State, the qualifications and disqualifications for membership of those Houses, the corrupt practices and other offenses at or in connection with such elections, and the decision of doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with such elections.
 
• This Act is a key piece of legislation that ensures free and fair elections in India.
 
• It has been amended multiple times to address various electoral issues and to strengthen the electoral process.
 
• The Act also provides for the appointment of election tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising out of or in connection with elections.
 
• Section 62 is specifically dedicated to the "Right to vote," outlining who is entitled to vote and who is disqualified from voting.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution mentions about establishing and maintaining institutions for religious and charitable purposes?

__
 
• **Article 26** of the Constitution of India mentions the freedom to manage religious affairs.
 
• It specifically states that every religious denomination or any section thereof shall have the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes.
 
• This article ensures that religious groups have the autonomy to manage their own affairs in matters of religion.
 
• It is part of the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution, ensuring religious freedom and the right to manage religious institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 26** is a crucial part of the Constitution, protecting the rights of religious denominations to maintain their own institutions and manage their own affairs.
 
• It is one of the fundamental rights provided under Part III of the Constitution, which deals with the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• This article helps in preserving the cultural and religious diversity of India by allowing religious groups to operate independently and maintain their traditions and practices.
 
• It complements other articles in the Constitution that provide for religious freedom and the right to practice and propagate religion.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is a _________landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**triangular**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a **triangular** landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
 
• It is one of the largest plateaus in India, covering an area of about 1.9 million square kilometers.
 
• The plateau is bounded by the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats, which converge at the southern tip of India.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is known for its rich mineral resources and diverse ecosystems.
 
• The region is characterized by its elevated terrain, with an average elevation ranging from 100 meters to 1,000 meters above sea level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Deccan Plateau extends over eight Indian states, including Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and parts of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is rich in volcanic soils, which are beneficial for agriculture, particularly for growing cotton and other crops.
 
• The region has a significant historical and cultural heritage, with many ancient temples, forts, and monuments.
 
• The plateau is also home to several major rivers, including the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, which are vital for irrigation and water supply in the region.
 
• The climate of the Deccan Plateau varies from arid and semi-arid in the northwest to more humid conditions in the southeast.

questions.question: In a situation wherein A (female) and B (male) are working in same office, same designation, same nature of work but unequal payment, which of the following Articles of the Constitution will be applicable?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39(d)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39(d)** of the Constitution of India mandates that the state shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
 
• This article falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• The DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• Article 39(d) aims to eliminate gender discrimination in terms of wage disparity and ensure economic justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21** of the Constitution of India guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• **Article 48A** deals with the protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife.
 
• **Article 18** abolishes titles except for military and academic distinctions.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, and they aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Although not enforceable by courts, these principles are crucial for governance and are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
